diagnosis: The image shows only one pair at the maximum within $10^{-9}$: its two points are the only non-rattlers, while the other 92 points have zero contacts at that threshold. The next $\sim$580 pairs form a plateau only $2$--$8\times10^{-8}$ below the maximum, so moving the isolated bottleneck pair can gain at most that gap before other pairs become maximal, explaining the shrinking $10^{-7}$--$10^{-8}$ improvements. With $94\times12=1128$ tangent degrees of freedom, a genuinely jammed local optimum should have a rigid, approximately isostatic contact graph with hundreds of equalised contacts and typically $\mathcal O(12)$ contacts per point, not $0$ or $1$. The incumbent is therefore missing a tightly equalised, spanning contact network; successive programs start from it and polish the same basin, repeatedly shaving the plateau without changing its near-contact topology, while larger attempted rearrangements have timed out.
